themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 18 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 3.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% increase (z-score: 6.76)—signaling a potential acute exposure event or disclosure wave in Sunset Park's aging housing stock.
evidence: 18 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% increase)
Z-score of 6.76 indicates statistically extreme spike
Sunset Park has substantial pre-1978 housing stock vulnerable to lead hazards
Lead exposure poses serious developmental and cognitive risks to children
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Department and HPD to identify which buildings/blocks triggered complaints and whether a remediation campaign is underway
Interview affected residents, particularly families with young children, about exposure concerns and access to testing
Investigate whether landlords are being held accountable for lead abatement under Local Law 1

themes_detail.label: Dead tree outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 21 THIS WEEK compared to 3.0 weekly average—a 600% spike (z-score: 5.92)—suggesting either storm damage, disease outbreak, or deferred park maintenance in Sunset Park.
evidence: 21 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average (600% increase)
Z-score of 5.92 indicates statistically extreme spike
Community Board has standing request for expanded parks/amenities
Potential link to recent weather or tree disease pattern
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine whether recent storms caused widespread damage or if disease is spreading
Map the geographic distribution of complaints to identify whether specific parks or blocks are affected
Report on Parks' tree maintenance budget and turnaround time for removal/replanting in CD 307

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendor crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1,100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—indicating either new enforcement activity, vendor proliferation, or resident frustration with street vending.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically anomalous event
No prior warning or news coverage suggests sudden change rather than known policy shift
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and Department of Consumer Affairs to clarify whether enforcement priorities changed this week
Interview affected street vendors about compliance issues and operating conditions
Assess whether residents are reporting specific health/safety concerns or general complaints about street vending

themes_detail.label: Smoking/vaping in residential areas
themes_detail.summary: Smoking and vaping complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 400% spike (z-score: 5.66)—reflecting emerging resident frustration with secondhand smoke exposure in buildings or shared spaces.
evidence: 5 smoking/vaping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% increase)
Z-score of 5.66 indicates statistically significant spike
Suggests concentrated incident or pattern in specific buildings
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints are concentrated in public housing, private buildings, or outdoor spaces
Interview residents about secondhand smoke exposure and enforcement of smoke-free policies
Contact Housing Authority or building management about enforcement and remediation efforts

themes_detail.label: Residential noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints reached 84 LAST WEEK versus 51.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 62% increase (z-score: 7.51)—suggesting either new noise sources, density pressure, or summer uptick in Sunset Park.
evidence: 84 noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 51.8 weekly average (62% increase)
Z-score of 7.51 indicates statistically extreme spike
Residential noise is top-3 complaint category overall (721 complaints in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Department of Environmental Protection to determine whether noise source is identifiable (construction, bars, transit, etc.)
Survey residents about specific times and sources of noise disturbance
Assess whether spike correlates with weather, seasonal activity, or new construction/development
